reasoning_traces.think:
The four bugs expose a fundamental mismatch between academic idealism and industrial pragmatism. BUG1 exploits a closed-form shortcut that introduces persistent bias in low-count regimes—exactly where sports betting margins matter most. BUG2&3 reveal that overdispersion parameters are often hard-coded rather than estimated, leading to systematic underestimation of uncertainty. BUG4 highlights the fragility of ad-hoc thresholds without rigorous empirical validation. Together, they form a coherent failure mode: assuming global statistical properties hold locally, ignoring heteroskedasticity, and relying on cookbook recipes instead of data-driven calibration. Fixing these requires moving from point estimates to posterior distributions, from plug-in estimators to hierarchical models, and from generic rules to context-specific priors.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The Anscombe transform dates to 1948, designed for variance stabilization in Poisson data. Negative binomial models emerged in genetics (1949) and became standard in ecology. James-Stein shrinkage originated in decision theory (1956). The Shin-de-vigoration method was introduced in finance (2003) for currency markets and adapted to sports betting in 2015. These tools were never designed for real-time, high-frequency prediction but have been retrofitted through community-driven innovation.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Bookmakers act as risk managers who balance profit targets with market competition. They use heuristics like fixed dispersions because recalibration costs time and money. Bettors, conversely, seek exploitable inefficiencies and may overreact to small-sample fluctuations. Our role is to build a rational agent model that outperforms both by exploiting their systematic errors.
